title: Protection for Customers of Home-based or Micro Businesses
what_it_is: Protection for Customers of Home-based or Micro Businesses

sections.label: Redress for misrepresentation under CPFTA
sections.summary: Misrepresentation is an unfair practice under CPFTA; consumers may seek help from CASE, the Small Claims Tribunal, or CCCS, which can seek a Court injunction.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Misrepresentation of goods and services constitutes an unfair practice under CPFTA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Consumers may approach the Consumers Association of Singapore (CASE) for assistance in seeking redress from suppliers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: If negotiation or mediation fails, consumers may file a claim with the Small Claims Tribunal or seek other forms of legal redress.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: In egregious cases, CASE will refer errant suppliers to the Competition and Consumer Commission of Singapore (CCCS) for investigation under CPFTA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: CCCS may then apply for a Court injunction to restrain the supplier from engaging in the unfair practice.

sections.label: Unregistered home-based business claims route
sections.summary: If a home-based business is not registered with ACRA, the only way forward is the Small Claims Tribunal, an online self-help platform costing up to $25.50.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As I understand it, if the home-based business is not registered with ACRA, the only way forward is through the Small Claims Tribunal and it is an online self-help platform costing up to $25.50 for a Court application.

sections.label: Voluntary Compliance Agreement with suppliers
sections.summary: With reasonable grounds to believe a supplier engaged in an unfair practice, the company is asked to enter a VCA undertaking not to repeat it and to compensate affected consumers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: If we feel that there are reasonable grounds to believe that the supplier/business has engaged in an unfair practice, we will ask the company to enter into a VCA.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: This is serious because this includes an undertaking that the business would not engage in the unfair practice and would also require the business to compensate any consumer who has suffered loss or damage as a result of the unfair practice and, in fact, we will require them to indicate that in the invoice that they issue to their customers.
